requirements.requirement: Configure opsadmin on node1 for SSH access with the specified ed25519 public key
requirements.summary: opsadmin user created and the exact requested ed25519 key installed into /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys with correct ownership (opsadmin:opsadmin) and permissions (700/600). Verified present and unchanged both before and after the node restart.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based SSH authentication (disable password/interactive auth)
requirements.summary: An sshd drop-in (/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-key-only.conf) sets PubkeyAuthentication yes and disables PasswordAuthentication, KbdInteractiveAuthentication, ChallengeResponseAuthentication, and PermitEmptyPasswords. Config validated with sshd -t, reloaded, and effective settings confirmed via sshd -T. A live SSH connection attempt forcing PreferredAuthentications=password was rejected, offering only publickey/gssapi, both before and after the restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol demonstrating healthy baseline, restart, and recovery on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (98aa35f5-...) matches the global before-prepare boot-identity snapshot and shows sshd active with the key and config in place. systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged, followed by connection timeouts consistent with a bounded outage, then a new boot_id (cc9377da-...) was observed matching the global after-executor snapshot. Post-restart checks confirm sshd active, authorized_keys intact, key-only config intact, effective sshd -T settings unchanged, and password-auth still rejected, demonstrating a full healthy-baseline -> disruption -> recovery transition.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — installing the specified ed25519 key for opsadmin and enforcing key-based-only SSH authentication — are directly and repeatedly verified via configuration inspection, sshd -T effective settings, and live SSH authentication attempts, both before and after a full node restart. The mandatory restart evidence protocol is also fully satisfied: boot identity changed as expected, cross-checked against the fixed global snapshots, with sshd, the key, and the config confirmed intact post-recovery. One minor, fully reverted troubleshooting mutation (a throwaway /tmp/keytest directory) was found but caused no lasting hygiene impact.
limitations: The after_prepare phase is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state cannot be independently distinguished beyond the executor comparison already provided.

No evidence was captured of an actual successful key-based login as opsadmin (only the negative test that password auth is rejected); this is a minor gap since positive pubkey-auth capability is strongly implied by the correctly configured authorized_keys and sshd settings but not directly demonstrated by a successful authenticated session.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all executor commands were either core task actions (user/key/sshd-config creation) or read-only discovery/verification, all clearly tied to satisfying the task or the restart evidence protocol. One unnecessary, low-risk troubleshooting mutation occurred: cmd-20e9df76971f4429 created /tmp/keytest with an incomplete/placeholder private-key file as part of an abandoned test approach before pivoting to a different (successful) password-rejection test; this was immediately and fully reverted via `rm -rf /tmp/keytest` in cmd-4d572619c4864177, leaving no residue (confirmed by identical /tmp contents, modulo boot-specific systemd paths, in the after-executor snapshot). Global lifecycle snapshots show no unexpected failed services, no unsafe new listening sockets, and healthy package state before and after.
